what_its_for: Solifenacin is used to treat an overactive bladder. It helps reduce the sudden urge to urinate, decreases how often you need to urinate, and can help prevent accidental leakage of urine (urge incontinence). It works by relaxing the bladder muscle so your bladder can hold more urine.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 5 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose to 10 mg once daily if needed and if you are tolerating the medication well. Some patients with kidney or liver problems may need a lower dose or should not take the higher dose. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and just take your next scheduled dose. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store solifenacin at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in a dry place such as a cabinet — not in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of caffeine or alcohol, as these can worsen bladder symptoms. Be careful in hot weather or during exercise because this medication can reduce your ability to sweat and may increase your risk of overheating. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you, as it may cause blurred vision or dizziness. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about all other medications you take, especially antifungal medicines like ketoconazole, as they can increase solifenacin levels in your body.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: difficulty urinating or cannot urinate at all; severe stomach pain or constipation; fast or irregular heartbeat; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing; severe dizziness or fainting; eye pain or sudden vision changes (signs of increased eye pressure). Also contact your doctor if you develop confusion, especially if you are an older adult.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your bladder symptoms within the first 1 to 2 weeks. However, it may take up to 4 to 8 weeks to feel the full benefit of this medication. Be patient and continue taking it as directed, even if you do not notice improvement right away. Talk to your doctor if your symptoms do not improve after several weeks.
special_populations: Older adults (over 65): Use with caution as older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as confusion, dizziness, and constipation. Kidney or liver problems: Patients with moderate to severe kidney or liver disease should not take the 10 mg dose; your doctor will determine the right dose for you. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Safety has not been clearly established. Talk to your doctor before taking this medication if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Children: Solifenacin tablets are generally not approved for use in children; VESIcare LS oral suspension is approved for certain children 2 years and older for a specific bladder condition — ask your doctor for guidance.
